papers.title: The (right) homotopy between two A$_{\infty}$-morphisms
papers.abstract: Let $f$, $g\colon A\to B$ be two A$_{\infty}$-morphisms between two A$_{\infty}$-algebras (linear over a commutative ring $\mathbb{K}$). In this paper, we compare different notions of (right) homotopy between $f$ and $g$. We note that the A$_{\infty}$-algebra $B\otimes R$, where $R:=\mathbb{K}[t,dt]$, is a model for the interval $[0,1]\times B$ in the sense of Fukaya-Oh-Ohta-Ono, and we give a short alternative proof, in the unfiltered case, of the existence of comparison morphisms between such models. We use it to prove that two A$_{\infty}$-morphisms are homotopic \`a la Seidel if and only if, considered as morphisms of 2-colored DG operads, they are elementary homotopic \`a la Markl-Shnider-Stasheff through a homotopy which is constant on the two monochromatic parts. We also provide an example of two A$_{\infty}$-morphisms which are elementary homotopic but not weakly equivalent (and so homotopic \`a la Seidel). Moreover, over a field, we observe that the models for the interval are good path objects in the category of A$_{\infty}$-algebras with (non strict) A$_{\infty}$-morphisms, and we explain why weakly equivalent A$_{\infty}$-morphisms need not be homotopic.

papers.title: Gorenstein cotorsion pairs induced by balanced pairs
papers.abstract: Let $(\mathcal{X},\mathcal{Y})$ be an admissible balanced pair in a locally presentable abelian category $\mathcal{A}$, and let $\mathcal{E}$ be its induced exact structure. We study the class $G(\mathcal{X})$ of cycles of two-sided complexes with terms in $\mathcal{X}$ that are both right and left $\mathcal{X}$-acyclic. If $\mathcal{X}$ is closed under direct summands and finite direct sums and is $\kappa$-Kaplansky for every sufficiently large regular cardinal $\kappa$, we prove that $(G(\mathcal{X}),G(\mathcal{X})^{\perp *})$ is a hereditary cotorsion pair relative to $\mathcal E$. For relative purity determined by finitely presented modules, we give two criteria for functorial completeness and show that relative periodic modules generate a functorially complete hereditary cotorsion pair. We also compute the relative Gorenstein objects, their right orthogonal, and explicit approximations for a family of exact structures over Dedekind domains.

papers.title: The Haagerup VOA at $c=8$
papers.abstract: We announce an explicit construction of a unitary, strongly rational vertex operator algebra $U$ of central charge $8$ inside $V_{E_6\oplus A_2}$, with a ribbon equivalence $\mathrm{Rep}(U)\simeq Z(\mathcal H_3)$ realizing the Haagerup double. The vertex algebra is generated by six affine currents and three specified weight-two fields; its weight-one Lie algebra is $\mathfrak{sl}_2\oplus\mathfrak{sl}_2$, at levels $1$ and $39$. We outline the argument, which combines exact lattice calculations, an all-weight strong-generation induction and $C_2$-cofiniteness, semisimple descent for a full corner of Zhu's algebra, modular Galois symmetry, and holomorphic $E_8$ extensions.

papers.title: Learning Transfers: Kan Extensions of Topological Invariants of Learned Representations
papers.abstract: When a learned representation is reused for a new task, which of its structure should survive? A task is a small category, a change of task is a functor $J$, and the invariants of a trained representation form a functor $F$. The left Kan extension $\operatorname{Lan}_JF$ is the invariant that the source and the change of task force on the target: by its universal property, every comparison of the source with an observed target invariant factors through it. The transfer discrepancy is the largest distance, over the target objects, between this extension and the observed invariant. For persistent homology the extension is a cokernel over comma categories, and a functorial version of the discrepancy, which also compares the maps between target objects, is $1$-Lipschitz under interleavings. On finite samples the discrepancy is a bottleneck distance, computed without approximation. For data glued from two pieces whose exclusive parts lie farther apart than the filtration scale, a Mayer-Vietoris sequence identifies what extending homology loses, while extending chains loses nothing. For a merge of labelled point clouds, the degree-zero discrepancy vanishes if and only if some $1$-Lipschitz classifier has a margin above the filtration scale at every sample point. In experiments on sampled manifolds, trained encoders and pretrained image models, every exact prediction holds on every sample. The discrepancy of truncated invariants recovers a hidden merge of separated parts far above chance and tells the intended target of a merge from a permuted control, but across pretrained models it does not track the accuracy of a linear probe.

papers.title: Projective Geometries as $\mathbb{F}_1$-modules
papers.abstract: We describe a fully faithful embedding of the category of axiomatic projective geometries into $\mathbb{F}_1$-modules, in the sense of Connes and Consani. In particular, the collineation group of a geometry is isomorphic to the group of automorphisms of its associated $\mathbb{F}_1$-module. Along the way, we describe a version of the classifying space construction for a broad generalization of Abelian groups which we call plasmas. Our construction subsumes Segal's existing delooping constructions for Abelian groups, commutative monoids and partial commutative monoids.

papers.title: Galois actions on surfaces and a higher genus Grothendieck-Teichm\"uller group
papers.abstract: We construct a modular operad $\mathbf{S}$ of mapping class groupoids modelling the higher-genus Teichm\"uller tower, with compositions and contractions encoding surface gluing. We prove a presentation theorem for maps out of $\mathbf{S}$ using genus-zero and genus-one generators and relations. Applying the work of Nakamura--Schneps, we obtain a faithful action of their subgroup $\widehat{\Gamma}\subseteq \widehat{\mathsf{GT}}$ on $\widehat{\mathbf{S}}$, and hence a faithful Galois action. The genus-zero truncation identifies with the cyclic operad of parenthesized ribbon braids, whose object-fixing profinite automorphism group is $\widehat{\mathsf{GT}}$. The completed classifying spaces form a modular $\infty$-operad whose corolla values are geometric \'etale homotopy types of moduli stacks of curves with nonzero tangent vectors at their marked points. The $\widehat{\Gamma}$-action induces a faithful action by homotopy automorphisms on the associated tower of profinite homotopy $1$-types, which agrees with the \'etale model in genus zero and one.

papers.title: The Burnside ring of simple $\mathcal{C}$-sets
papers.abstract: The Burnside ring of a finite category, introduced by Webb, generalizes the classical Burnside ring of a finite group. However, unlike the classical case, the Burnside ring of a finite category has finite rank if and only if the category is equivalent to a groupoid. In this article, we introduce a new invariant associated with a finite category $\mathcal{C}$, called the \emph{simple Burnside ring} of $\mathcal{C}$ and denoted by $B^S(\mathcal{C})$. This construction is obtained from simple $\mathcal{C}$-sets and generalizes the classical Burnside ring of a finite group. Moreover, the ring $B^S(\mathcal{C})$ always has finite rank. We develop the basic theory of simple $\mathcal{C}$-sets and study several structural properties of the ring $B^S(\mathcal{C})$. In particular, we determine all ring homomorphisms from $B^S(\mathcal{C})$ to $\mathbb{Z}$, describe its prime spectrum, and obtain a decomposition theorem expressing $B^S(\mathcal{C})$ as a product of simple Burnside rings of strongly connected subcategories.
